full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the opposite-party No. 1, Zayedul Haque as plaintiff, instituted SCC. Suit No. 106 of 2008 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka against the petitioners, as defendant, for a decree of ejectment. The suit was decreed on 2-5-2012 on the sole ground that the tenant-petitioners are defaulter. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court the present petitioners filed Civil Revision No. 1467 of 2012 before this Court and obtained Rule and order of stay. 

 3. The matter was heard and by the judgment and decree dated 15-9-2015 a Single Bench of this Court presided by Mr. Justice Sharif Uddin Chaklader discharged the Rule. Thereafter, the petitioners came with this application under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code praying for review of the judgment and obtained the present Rule and order of status-quo. 

 6. Heard the learned Advocate for the review petitioners have gone through the application, annexures thereto and the impugned judgment and decree passed by this Court and the exhibits referred by the petitioners. 

 8. From the annexure, it appears that the said amount was deposited by the petitioners by a single Challan No. 4059 dated 17-9-2005. Judgment and decree passed by the trial court as well as by this Court discharging the Rule concurrently found that the defendants did not pay rents from January, 2006 to March, 2006 in House Rent Control Case No. 05 of 2001. Moreover, they deposited rent for August, 2005 to January, 2006 by a single Challan No. 4059 at a time which goes to show that the defendants are defaulter and the payment made by them in lump for 06(six) months' cannot safe the petitioners from the category of defaulter. 

 9. A review of the judgment may be sought for short only on the Aground that from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made or on account of some mistakes or error apparent on the face of the record, but in the instant case this Court finds no error on the face of the judgment or record and nothing new could be discovered by the petitioners to show that they are not defaulter and the observations made by this Court is contrary to the actual state of facts and evidences on record, as such, this Court finds no merit in the Rule seeking review of the judgment passed by this Court.
